#ETH I once used only my available 1000 U, and by rolling positions through contracts, I made 100,000 U within 3 months. Today I won’t talk about “getting rich overnight”—I’ll just explain how to survive in this high-risk arena and take your profits with you.
1. The core logic of rolling 100x in 3 months
At first, I tested with 300 USD, opening only 10 USD worth of 100x leverage contracts each time. The appeal of 100x leverage is that when you’re right on direction, a 1% gain can effectively double your principal.
2. Five life-saving rules
Before every trade, you must silently repeat them—violate even once and you stop trading.
1. Cut losses immediately if wrong—never hold and hope: Contract trading hates “luck/hope.” Early on, I was liquidated twice because I kept hard-holding thinking it would bounce back. Later I set a rule: once you hit the stop-loss level, close the position immediately no matter how unwilling you feel, even if the market reverses afterward—you must not regret it. Remember: in contracts, staying alive matters 100 times more than proving you were “right.”
2. Stop after 20 consecutive mistakes—never touch contracts that day: There’s always “unreasonable” market behavior, and continuous losses can crush your mindset, leading you to make even more errors. I set a “circuit breaker”: if you make 20 consecutive wrong trades in a single day, I immediately shut down the software and don’t trade again that day, no matter how tempting the opportunity looks. After a cold night and a fresh look, you’ll often be able to avoid even greater risks.
3. Withdraw when you reach 5000 USD—never let greed take over: Greed when you’re winning is more deadly than panic when you’re losing. My rule is: when your account profit reaches 5000 USD, you must withdraw at least half of the gains. When I traded ETH in a one-direction market, I started with 500 USD and rolled it to 500,000 within 3 days. Along the way, I withdrew 200,000. That helped me preserve most of my profits during subsequent pullbacks, so I didn’t “ride a roller coaster” all the way back to zero like other people.
4. Trade only single-direction trends—play dead during ranging/sideways markets: The key to making money with contracts is “riding the trend.” In a choppy, ranging market, 100x leverage is basically a death lever.
5. Never risk more than 10% of your principal per entry: Even if the opportunity feels extremely certain, you can’t go all-in. With a light position, no matter how wild the volatility gets, your mindset won’t collapse—you’ll have the confidence to wait for the trend to unfold. Going all-in is pointless even if you’re right 9 times; being wrong once can wipe you out.
Many souls fall along the crypto road, but only the honest catch the fish song across the river—🈶 For those with backbone!

二、5条保命铁律
每次开单前必须默念，违反一次就停盘。
1. 错了立马割肉，绝不扛单：合约交易最忌讳“侥幸心理”。我早期两次爆仓，都是因为“觉得会反弹”而硬扛。后来定下铁律：到了止损位，不管多不甘心都立即平仓，哪怕之后行情反转也不后悔。要记住，在合约里，活下来比“证明自己正确”重要100倍。
2. 连续错20次就停手，当天绝不碰合约：行情总有“不讲理”的时候，连续亏损会让人心态崩溃，越操作错得越多。我设了“熔断机制”：单日连续错20次就立刻关掉软件，当天再诱人的机会也不动手。冷静一夜后再看，往往能避开更大的风险。
3. 赚到5000美金必须提现，绝不上头：赚钱时的贪心比亏损时的恐慌更致命。我规定：账户盈利到5000美金，至少要提走一半利润。去ETH单边行情，我从500美金起步，3天滚到50万，中途提了20万出来，这让我在后续回调时保住了大半利润，没像别人那样“过山车”般回到起点。
4. 只做单边趋势，震荡期装死：合约赚钱的核心是“借势”，震荡行情中100倍杠杆如同送命杠杆。

title: Epic Chain是什么？从NFT爆款项目到RWA+AI时代的新一代以太坊Layer 2
subTitle:
过去几年，区块链行业经历了从DeFi、NFT到RWA（现实世界资产）的不断演变。
而曾经专注数字收藏品和娱乐IP领域的Ethernity Chain（ERN），也正在迎来一次重要升级——Epic Chain（EPIC）。
Epic Chain被视为Ethernity生态发展的新阶段，通过社区治理推动升级，获得了超过97%的社区支持，正式迈向以太坊Layer 2基础设施方向。
如今的Epic Chain，不再只是一个NFT平台，而是希望打造一个结合RWA、娱乐产业、AI安全技术以及Web3应用生态的新型区块链网络。

Epic Chain是什么？
简单来说，Epic Chain是一条基于以太坊Layer 2技术打造的区块链网络，目标是为现实资产、娱乐内容以及数字IP提供更加高效、安全的链上基础设施。
相比传统区块链应用，Epic Chain希望解决几个核心问题：
交易速度不足；链上成本较高；娱乐行业数字资产管理困难；Web2用户进入Web3门槛较高。
通过Layer 2技术，Epic Chain能够在继承以太坊安全性的同时，提高交易效率并降低使用成本，让更多商业应用能够进入区块链生态。

Epic Chain有哪些核心优势？
1、专注RWA与娱乐产业
Epic Chain的重要方向之一，就是推动现实世界资产和娱乐内容进入区块链。
未来，影视作品、体育IP、品牌资产、数字收藏品等内容，都可以通过区块链技术实现更加透明的管理和流通。
这意味着传统娱乐产业可以拥有新的商业模式，例如数字版权管理、粉丝经济以及IP资产数字化。

2、AI增强安全体系
随着Web3应用不断扩大，安全问题也越来越受到关注。
Epic Chain结合AI相关技术，希望提升网络安全能力，包括风险检测、智能监控以及对异常行为的识别。
通过AI与区块链结合，Epic Chain希望打造更加安全可靠的数字资产环境。

3、支持Web3应用开发
Epic Chain不仅面向普通用户，也为开发者提供基础设施支持。
开发者可以基于网络构建各种应用，包括：
NFT项目；游戏生态；数字身份系统；娱乐内容平台；RWA相关应用。
通过降低开发门槛，Epic Chain希望吸引更多项目进入生态。

EPIC代币有什么作用？
EPIC是Epic Chain生态的重要代币。
它主要用于：
网络生态参与：
用户可以使用EPIC参与生态活动，并支持链上应用运行。
治理功能：
代币持有者可以参与社区治理，对生态发展方向提出建议或参与投票。
生态激励：
EPIC也可以作为生态奖励工具，用于激励开发者、用户以及社区贡献者。
随着生态不断发展，代币的实际应用场景也将成为影响其价值的重要因素。

为什么Epic Chain值得关注？
Epic Chain的发展方向，正好契合当前区块链行业的几个热门趋势：
第一，RWA资产上链趋势不断增强。
越来越多传统资产开始探索区块链化，未来可能带来新的市场机会。
第二，娱乐产业正在寻找Web3解决方案。
数字版权、IP价值释放以及用户互动模式，都可能成为区块链的重要应用场景。
第三，Layer 2成为以太坊扩展的重要方向。
随着以太坊生态持续发展，高性能、低成本的Layer 2网络需求不断增加。

需要注意哪些风险？
虽然Epic Chain拥有清晰的发展方向，但项目未来仍然面临挑战。
包括：
生态应用增长速度；开发者和用户数量；实际商业合作落地情况；Layer 2赛道竞争压力。

What Is Glamsterdam? Ethereum’s Next Major Upgrade Explained

The Glamsterdam upgrade is planned for the second half of 2026. In an X post, $SSV Network said developers are working toward Q4, although Ethereum has not confirmed a mainnet date. The planned changes could reshape block production, prepare parallel processing and update network costs.

Ethereum’s official roadmap uses the broader H2 2026 window. Final specifications, client readiness, security reviews and public-testnet results would determine when the upgrade reaches mainnet.

Ethereum’s next upgrade has a practical constraint:

Fit more work into a 12-second slot without pushing home operators out.
It is called Glamsterdam.

Gloas covers the consensus side while Amsterdam covers the execution side.

Core developers are working toward Q4 2026. More… pic.twitter.com/sBxeWdQuSc
— $SSV Network (@ssv_network) July 28, 2026
What Is Glamsterdam and Why Does Testing Matter?
The name Glamsterdam combines Gloas, the consensus-layer upgrade named after a star, with Amsterdam, the execution-layer upgrade named after a former Devconnect host city. Gloas updates validator coordination and consensus, while Amsterdam changes transaction and smart contract execution. Together, they form one Ethereum network upgrade.
In May, the Ethereum Foundation said a multi-client devnet had tested the external-builder pipeline across nearly all clients. Developers also aligned on a credible post-Glamsterdam gas-limit target of 200 million.
The 200 million gas-limit floor is a post-Glamsterdam target, not a current mainnet result. Before announcing a mainnet fork date, developers plan to stabilize a complete devnet, release compatible clients, finish security reviews and confirm that public testnets are stable.
How Will ePBS Change Ethereum Block Production?
Most Ethereum proposers rely on external builders to assemble execution payloads. Trusted relays help manage the handoff between builders and validators. EIP-7732 would move the basic process into Ethereum’s consensus rules.#Write2Earn $ETH

title: The Investor You Become Matters More Than the Portfolio You Build.
subTitle:
Many people begin investing to grow their wealth. And that's a worthwhile goal. But over time, something else happens. The market teaches lessons that go beyond money. It teaches patience when results take longer than expected.
It teaches humility when we're wrong. It teaches discipline when emotions are high. It teaches resilience when markets become difficult.
The longer you invest, the more you realize: A portfolio is not the only thing being built. Your habits are being built. Your character is being built. Your decision-making is being built.
🔑 Key Takeaway: The greatest return from investing may not be financial. It may be becoming a wiser, more disciplined person.
🧠 Practical Reflection; As an investor, ask yourself: "Am I only growing my portfolio, or am I also growing my patience, discipline, and wisdom?"
Because markets come and go. But the person you become remains.
Systems over emotion. Conviction over noise.

11 years. Countless innovations.

From the genesis block to becoming the backbone of DeFi, NFTs, Layer 2s, and countless onchain innovations, $ETH has changed crypto forever.

Happy 11th birthday, Ethereum. Here's to what's next. 🚀

#Ethereum #ETH #Crypto #Web3 #DeFi

#ETH 
As Crypto Perpetual Futures Boom, Ethereum’s Role Is Shifting

The explosive growth of crypto perpetual futures is quietly redrawing Ethereum’s role in market structure. Traders chasing low latency and deep liquidity are migrating to layer-2 networks, and a growing number of builders now argue that Ethereum shouldn’t try to compete as an execution layer. Instead, it should double down on what it already does best: anchoring the security and settlement of the L2s where the real action is happening, according to the original CoinDesk report.

That position reflects a pragmatic turn. For years, Ethereum’s roadmap battled criticism over speed and cost. High-frequency perps trading never fit naturally on a chain prioritizing decentralization over throughput. Rollups and validiums flipped the script. Now, protocols like Arbitrum, Optimism, and zkSync handle order matching and execution, while Ethereum secures the final state. The arrangement solves the UX problem without requiring Ethereum to match the performance of Solana or Sui. The payoff for traders is sharper: sub-cent fees and confirmation times measured in milliseconds on some L2s, while still benefiting from Ethereum’s deep liquidity pools and battle-tested security.

The pivot carries real economic weight. Perps are the single largest category by volume in crypto. When that volume migrates off mainnet, Ethereum loses direct fee capture. L2 batches settle in chunks, compressing thousands of trades into a single data blob posted to mainnet. The network earns less per transaction on the immediate count but arguably strengthens its long-term moat by feeding a whole ecosystem of application-specific chains that pay for security. It’s a bet on scale over unit economics—similar to the cloud infrastructure playbook where margins are thin at the base layer but enormous in aggregate. That logic, however, isn’t yet fully priced into how analysts value Ethereum’s fee generation. #Write2Earn $ETH

Iranian fast boats block the Strait of Hormuz! BTC $64,576 is set to trigger a risk-off breakout

In one sentence
Iranian naval fast boats launched a sudden strike to blockade the Strait of Hormuz, rapidly escalating geopolitical tensions. The direct demand for risk aversion funds is clearly bullish for BTC and ETH.

What happened
Guys, the gunpowder smell in the Middle East is getting thick again. This time, Iran didn’t play games—it directly deployed a bunch of military fast boats to block the Strait of Hormuz. Plainly put, this move is both cheap and annoying: no matter how strong your navy fleet is, it can’t handle a bunch of small boats weaving in and out along the key shipping lanes. The Strait of Hormuz is the lifeline for global oil transport—nearly one-third of the world’s seaborne crude oil goes through it. Iran is determined to choke the vital artery with this kind of asymmetric tactic and effectively flips the table of global diplomatic maneuvering. The international crude oil market instantly exploded. This kind of concrete armed blockade is far more serious than just “tough talk.” Once diplomacy completely breaks down, the global supply chain will inevitably take a major hit.

Market impact
At this level of geopolitical “black swan,” the most immediate response is in traditional finance and risk assets.

In the short term, risk-off sentiment spikes instantly. A surge in global oil prices will inevitably raise inflation expectations, and traditional stock markets—especially—will be the first to get hit with sell-offs. Meanwhile, crypto markets are relatively independent right now: BTC and ETH’s correlation with traditional risk assets could be disrupted. Once traditional finance panics due to geopolitics, large capital needs to find high-liquidity safe-haven assets. This risk-off capital flowing into the market is a real positive for BTC and ETH.

In the medium term, if the situation drags on in a stalemate, global liquidity expectations will likely reverse. Geopolitical conflict will force some institutions to readjust asset allocations, using crypto assets as an effective tool to hedge geopolitical risk. This sentiment shift will further solidify BTC and ETH’s bottom support.

My take

#baby $BABY Babylon’s story, which relies on “bitcoin-native staking,” has definitely brought expectations to their peak. It allows BTC players to get PoS chain rewards directly without having to hassle with cross-chain transfers—and this hardcore move truly lives up to the “BTC security network” title. So far, the mainnet has also successfully wooed top industry heavyweights like Allnodes, Figment, and Galaxy Digital to show up and back the project. At first glance, the foundation looks quite stable.

But if you dig into the entry manual for the Finality Providers (FPs), you’ll find the waters are very deep. The bar is set absolutely absurdly high: you have to grind through the testnet, handle the tedious KYB identity verification, and then be very strict about submitting the PR according to the timeline. Miss the registration and you’re out. Even worse, after the network switches to phase two, everyone must tear everything down and re-certify. Over 200 teams are competing for those 60 active seats that can vote. And players holding bitcoin don’t even have the right to freely choose nodes—they can only operate within the project’s pre-selected “curated list.” This isn’t truly a permissionless free-for-all competition—it’s more like an officially led license allocation.@babylonlabs_io 

If you follow these rules, social stratification becoming locked in is almost a foregone conclusion. Right now, giants like Allnodes, Figment, Galaxy Digital, Luganodes, P2P, and Stakefish have long scooped up staking capital from the market thanks to their scale and footprint. Everyone invests just to stay safe, so naturally they funnel coins into big institutions. Once this kind of Matthew effect takes hold, the winner-takes-all situation can’t be contained. As long as a few top players among the 60 quietly coordinate with each other, the power to provide block finality confirmation becomes dough in their hands—they can shape it however they want.

In short, Babylon wears the geeky cloak of “no trust” in crypto on the surface, but underneath it is a highly closed privilege club. No matter how rigorous the underlying code is, it can’t prevent capital cliques from banding together behind those 60 slots. Is this really adding an extra security lock to Bitcoin, or is it just handpicking and elevating a few monopoly oligarchs? Let the market find out for itself.$ETH #eth

I dug through 7 days of relay log data from the Babylon testnet and found that, on average, it drops a proof every 4 hours—

This week, I wrote a monitoring script and kept watching the Babylon testnet relay logs for 7 straight days. In total, I caught 43 instances of the error "Proof submission timeout." On average, every 4 hours there’s a Bitcoin transaction proof that isn’t submitted to the Babylon chain on time. $BABY 

As for what the relay does, I previously thought its job was just "to relay"—to read out the transaction information from the Bitcoin mainnet to the Babylon chain. But after digging through the logs, I realized it doesn’t just read it; it also verifies it. For every transaction sent from the Bitcoin mainnet, the relay runs SPV (simple payment verification) to confirm that the transaction was actually packaged, and then signs the verification result and submits it to the Babylon chain. This verification + signing process takes an average of 47 seconds. @babylonlabs_io #baby 

The problem is "verification timeout"—if the relay node network jitters, or if the Bitcoin mainnet blocks are delayed by more than 10 minutes, the relay marks that transaction as "pending" and retries every 15 minutes. But Babylon’s time-lock smart contract only accepts proofs from the first submission. If the first one times out, even if later retries succeed, it doesn’t help—your staked transaction gets stuck in a gray area: "on-chain but not yet verified." #ETH #BTC 

I simulated this scenario once: after submitting the staking signature, I manually shut off the relay network for 30 minutes and then restored it. The staking record on the Babylon chain showed the "pending" status for a full 2 hours until I manually triggered a verification retry, at which point it turned "confirmed."

So in my view, the "seamless experience" described in the whitepaper is a joke in the face of relay jitter.

My advice comes in two parts. If you’re only testing with a small amount, then if it gets stuck, just accept it—you might have to wait longer, but that’s it. If you’re planning to stake a large amount, you must avoid operating during periods of mainnet congestion (for example, when Bitcoin network Gas fees are over 100 sat/vB), because at that time the probability of relay timeouts doubles. Babylon’s official team says they’re working on a "relay redundancy pool" (running 3 relays in parallel). Once that goes live, you can go big again. For now, with only a single relay, reliability isn’t good enough.

#baby $BABY Last night I tested the TBV node on the Babylon testnet, and it completely broke my spirit over a tiny mechanism. The interface basically doesn’t give you any chance to input your own amount—you can only choose among three fixed tiers: 0.01, 0.1, and 1 BTC. At first I thought the web interaction wasn’t implemented well, so I dug into the underlying logic and confirmed this is a dead-lock mechanism that BitVM3 can’t avoid: garbled circuits (garbled circuit) require all transactions in the transaction tree to be fully signed in advance, so the amount options can only be made as “standard products.” This makes it feel extremely surreal: the front-end page looks as convenient and cutting-edge as DeFi, but at the bottom it’s still tightly trapped by Bitcoin Script’s rigid old rules. I ran the full flow using 0.01 signet BTC—done in three minutes. But if you want to try something non-standard like 0.05, the system simply tells you it’s not serving you.

BitVM3’s engineering optimizations are indeed impressive—it hard-cuts the on-chain friction of disputes to around 9 dollars. The original BitVM2 assertTx was a bulky 4.8MB; now it’s been condensed to 56KB. However, the fixed ticket settings create extremely imbalanced “claim books” for large funds versus small retail players. Let’s do the math: once something goes wrong, if I challenge with that 0.01 BTC, the 9-dollar cost is effectively like directly losing 2.5% of the principal. If instead an institution puts in 100 of them, the same defense fee would be only 0.0009%. In plain terms, this defense mechanism is basically a disguised punishment for small-cap players.

The time-cost math is even harder to quantify. At this stage, the challenge period still takes weeks to resolve disputes. Sure, on-chain gas consumption has been reduced, but the waiting period hasn’t decreased at all. If you’ve compared it to the validity proof in ZK (instant confirmation, no waiting), you’ll find TBV’s optimistic model is basically “patching holes with other holes”: to avoid huge on-chain computations, it just makes the user’s liquidity suffer in a time prison.

Once you peel back the layers, the conclusion is practically screaming out: this “fixed specs plus long lock-up period” setup is clearly a VIP zone prepared for big institutions and whales. The retail wish for true save-and-withdraw anytime is simply not on the current schedule. Even if the token burn mechanism of $BABY  is marketed with all the fancy hype, it can’t hide its underlying physical constraints. This wave of operations by @babylonlabs_io  looks like performing ruthless net asset value filtering. #eth  $ETH

I cracked Babylon’s slashing calculator code and worked out the true formula for that "dynamic ratio"

Last night I went through the Babylon slashing module simulator code three times and finally figured out how that "dynamic slashing ratio" is computed. The official whitepaper only says one line: "The slashing ratio dynamically adjusts based on network conditions," but the code contains a complete set of formulas:

Slashing ratio = Base slashing rate (2%) × Misbehavior severity coefficient (1–5x) × Network staked total amount coefficient (current stake / target stake) @babylonlabs_io 

I plugged in parameters from the Babylon testnet and ran the numbers. If the whole network has staked 5,000 BTC and a node double-signs, and the misbehavior severity coefficient is 3 (medium), then the slashing ratio is 2% × 3 × (5000/8000) = 3.75%. Not that high, right? But if the total staked amount is only 2,000 BTC, with the same severity coefficient, the slashing ratio jumps to 2% × 3 × (2000/8000) = 1.5%—the less staked, the lighter the penalty. The BABY design logic is "don’t scare people away when staking is low." But flip it around—early on, when network staking is low, the cost of misbehavior is also low, so nodes are actually more tempted to cause trouble. #baby 

I dug one layer deeper into the code and found a more detailed BABY setting: if the same node triggers slashing for a second time within 30 days, the misbehavior severity coefficient starts from 1 and jumps to 3. That means: the first accidental slip is 3.75%, but the second accidental slip is immediately 11.25%. I simulated two consecutive downtime-triggered slashing events on the Babylon testnet; the second time did result in a deduction of 11.2%, matching the code’s calculation exactly. #BTC #ETH $BABY 

The Babylon whitepaper says "slashing is capped at 20%," but the 20% is for a single extreme case (e.g., double-sign + network partition + staking saturation). For ordinary daily scenarios that most retail users encounter, the ratio is likely to fluctuate roughly between 2% and 5%.

So my conclusion is simple:
- If you only plan to stake 0.1–0.5 BTC for testing, the slashing risk is within a tolerable range (2%–5% won’t deduct much).
- If you plan to stake 1 BTC or more, make sure to distribute it across 3–5 different nodes—don’t put all your eggs in one basket—because a node’s second slashing doubles the penalty.
- And never run a node yourself. You’re not saving service fees—you’re increasing the probability that slashing gets triggered.

扒Babylon的罚没计算器代码，我算出了那个"动态比例"的真实公式

昨晚我把Babylon罚没模块的模拟器代码翻了三遍，终于搞懂那个"动态罚没比例"是怎么算出来的。官方白皮书里只写了一句话"罚没比例根据网络状况动态调整"，但代码里藏着一套完整公式：罚没比例 = 基础罚没率（2%）× 违纪严重系数（1-5倍）× 网络质押总量系数（当前质押量/目标质押量）@babylonlabs_io 

我拿babylon测试网的参数套进去算了一笔：如果全网质押了5000个BTC，某个节点双签，违纪严重系数取3（中等），罚没比例就是 2% × 3 ×（5000/8000）= 3.75%。看着不高对吧？但如果全网质押量只有2000个BTC，同样违纪系数，罚没比例直接飙到 2% × 3 ×（2000/8000）= 1.5%——质押量越少，罚得越轻。BABY这个设计的逻辑是"质押少的时候别把人吓跑"，但反过来想——网络早期质押量低，作恶成本也低，节点搞事的冲动反而更大。#baby 

我又往前追了一层代码，发现baby一个更细节的设定：如果同一个节点在30天内第二次触发罚没，违纪严重系数直接从1起步，跳升到3。也就是说，第一次手滑罚3.75%，第二次手滑直接罚11.25%。我在babylon测试网模拟了连续两次宕机触发罚没，第二次确实扣了11.2%，和代码算出来的一模一样。#BTC #ETH $BABY 

Babylon白皮书里写着"罚没上限20%"，但20%是给单次极端情况（比如双签+网络分裂+质押饱和）准备的。普通散户日常遇到的情况，大概率在2%-5%之间来回摩擦。

所以我的判断很简单，如果你只打算质押0.1-0.5个BTC做测试，罚没风险在可承受范围内（2%-5%扣不了多少）；
如果你准备质押1个BTC以上，务必分散到3-5个不同节点，别把鸡蛋放一个篮子里，因为单节点第二次罚没直接翻倍；
千万别自己跑节点，你不是在省服务费，你是在给自己增加触发罚没的概率。

That directly tears off the cover: to secure defense-oriented capital that’s aiming to safely earn interest and farm airdrops, there was never any real effort to send money into the application layer.

Ether, XRP flat as chip stocks steady on Samsung's 250-fold profit surge

Crypto's largest tokens were close to unchanged on Thursday as the semiconductor selloff that has driven markets for two weeks showed its first real sign of easing.

Ether traded at about $1,905 and bitcoin at $64,100, both flat on the day, with $XRP at $1.07, solana at $74, $BNB at $572 and TRON at 33 cents. Hyperliquid's $HYPE slipped to $54. Volumes were modest, with roughly $28 billion changing hands in bitcoin and $10 billion in ether.

Electronics giant Samsung said chip profit rose more than 250-fold on AI memory shortages, and the Kospi swung between a 6% gain and a 2% loss before settling, after a stretch that took the index down more than 40% from its June peak.

Samsung's reaction is the tell on how high the bar has become. Profit up 250-fold moved the shares 2%. SK Hynix reported profit up 557% on Wednesday and fell 17%. Results are not the problem, expectations are.

U.S. earnings split overnight. Microsoft gained nearly 9% in extended trading on its fastest cloud growth in four years, while Meta fell 8% on a weak revenue forecast. Nasdaq 100 futures rose 1% after the index entered a technical correction on Wednesday.

The weekly picture across crypto is deeper than Thursday's calm suggests. $HYPE is down 8% over seven sessions, the worst of the majors. xrp has lost 6%, solana 5%, dogecoin 4% to $0.07, and bitcoin 3%. $BNB is the only major holding a weekly gain, up marginally.

What stands out is how little of the equity turmoil has reached crypto. Bitcoin tracked semiconductor stocks through most of July, rising and falling with the chip trade.

It held through last Thursday's $797 billion drop in U.S. megacap technology, held through Korea's record two-day decline midweek, and is flat again now. Such softness across the alts looks more like thinning liquidity than a response to anything in equities.#Write2Earn $ETH $XRP

Data shows that the total value locked (TVL) of the three main networks—Optimism, Base, and Arbitrum—is currently about $4.8 billion, accounting for 96% of the entire L2 ecosystem.

The report noted that the decline in the L2 ecosystem coincides with challenges facing Ethereum overall. Since the beginning of this year, many top executives have left the Ethereum Foundation, and staffing adjustments have also been made. Meanwhile, as traditional financial institutions explore blockchain technology infrastructure, they have gradually begun to turn their attention toward alternatives beyond Ethereum.

For example, DTCC is working to enhance the tokenization of Treasury bonds in a multi-chain environment, and JPMorgan has expanded the JPM Coin to support multiple public chains. However, stablecoins still form an important pillar of the Ethereum ecosystem, as USDC and USDT are still settled primarily across Ethereum and its respective L2 networks, allowing Ethereum to continue playing the important bridge role in entering finance #ETH

content:
أخبار BlockBeats، في 29 يوليو، انخفض إجمالي القيمة المقفلة (TVL) للنظام البيئي لشبكة إيثيريوم Layer2 إلى حوالي 5 مليارات دولار، وهو أدنى مستوى له منذ عام 2023، مما أدى فعلياً إلى محو حجم الأموال التي تراكمت خلال فترة النمو السريع للنظام البيئي لـ L2 في عام 2024.

تُظهر البيانات أن إجمالي القيمة المقفلة (TVL) لشبكات Optimism وBase وArbitrum الثلاث الرئيسية يبلغ حالياً حوالي 4.8 مليار دولار، وهو ما يمثل 96% من إجمالي النظام البيئي لـ L2.

وأشار التقرير إلى أن تراجع النظام البيئي لـ L2 يتزامن مع التحديات التي تواجهها إيثيريوم بشكل عام. فمنذ بداية هذا العام، غادر العديد من كبار المسؤولين التنفيذيين مؤسسة إيثيريوم، كما تم إجراء تعديلات على الموظفين. وفي الوقت نفسه، وبينما تستكشف المؤسسات المالية التقليدية البنية التحتية لتقنية البلوكشين، فإنها بدأت تدريجياً في توجيه أنظارها نحو بدائل خارج نطاق إيثيريوم.

على سبيل المثال، تعمل شركة DTCC على تعزيز ترميز سندات الخزانة بناءً على بيئة متعددة السلاسل، كما قام بنك جي بي مورغان بتوسيع عملة JPM Coin لتشمل العديد من السلاسل العامة. ومع ذلك، لا تزال العملة المستقرة تشكل دعامة مهمة للنظام البيئي لإيثيريوم، حيث لا تزال عملتا USDC وUSDT تُسويان بشكل رئيسي عبر إيثيريوم وشبكات L2 الخاصة بها، مما يجعل إيثيريوم تواصل لعب دور الجسر المهم لدخول التمويل #ETH

#ETH The crypto world is crazy and unreasonable.
That night, Lao Zhang came to me for a smoke, his fingers shaking around the cigarette. He said he had stared at the market for three straight nights and, gritting his teeth, converted the spare cash he had saved for more than half a year into 7000U, wanting to try his hand in crypto. He was bored of stock trading, and people always say one day in crypto is a year in the real world, so he wanted to give it a shot!
Over the next five days, I let him witness the blazing speed of the crypto market. On the first day, his account was already up 30%, and at lunch he could still joke with me, saying, “This makes more money than running clients for half a month.” On the third day at 2 a.m., he sent me a message. The numbers in the screenshot had already nearly tripled, and his excitement was impossible to hide between the lines. By the afternoon of the fifth day, he suddenly called me on voice. In a strangely calm tone, he said he had just hit withdraw, and 300,000 RMB was already reflected in the bank card deposit notification.
Converted from 7000U, that was only a little over 50,000 yuan of principal, and in just five days he had pocketed 300,000. In any traditional industry, that kind of return is unthinkable. My older brother later told me that the moment he tapped the withdraw button, his back was covered in cold sweat, afraid it was all a dream.
He said that when he held this money in his hands, his first reaction was not ecstasy, but lingering fear. He had seen too many people in this kind of market make ten or twenty times their money, only to get greedy and use leverage, and lose even their principal overnight. So from the very beginning, he set himself a hard rule: once the target was reached, get out immediately, leaving no room for greed.
This story sounds like a legend, but only we know how many nights he stayed up over those five days, how many candlesticks he watched, and how many times he suppressed the urge to add to his position. The madness of crypto has never been about giving everyone money. It simply throws luck, judgment, and temperament into a brutal test in an extremely short amount of time. For my older brother to get out steadily this time, it was never because of gambler’s luck, but because he stayed clear-headed enough to hold onto his bottom line amid the madness.
Now my older brother is continuing to follow me with a fixed position of 100,000, and the next withdrawal target is 500,000

7000U换算过来也就五万多本金，五天时间直接落袋30万，这种收益放在任何传统行当里，想都不敢想。老哥哥后来跟我说，点下提现按钮的那一刻，他后背全是冷汗生怕是一场梦。
他说这钱拿在手里，第一反应不是狂喜，是后怕——他见过太多人在这种行情里赚了十倍二十倍，最后贪心加杠杆，一夜之间连本金都赔得精光。所以他从一开始就给自己定了死规矩：到了目标点位立刻撤，半分贪念都不能留。

My take is that

Brother, after reading Arthur Hayes’ latest long article, the more I read it, the more it feels like this guy’s words are prickly—yet his logic has no hard flaws.

Hayes ran the numbers: from November 2022 to this past mid-year, the AI crowd—data centers and infrastructure companies—issued about $1.5 trillion in debt. Coincidentally, that figure is almost the same as the amount of new money added to the US M2 over the same period. His conclusion is very straightforward: the newly minted dollars were all absorbed by AI, so Bitcoin doesn’t get a share of the “soup.” That’s why over the past two years liquidity has expanded, but BTC hasn’t pushed to new highs.

Now he has cleared most of his altcoins, keeping only $BTC  and $ETH. He also said BTC might first drop to around 40,000, then wait for the Federal Reserve to print again. Right now, $BTC  is hovering around 64,800, and it doesn’t rise even a single percentage point a day—so, yeah, it really does look like it’s waiting for the wind.

My take is that AI and crypto are going after the same pot of money. As long as the bubble doesn’t burst and the “water” isn’t released, it’s hard for BTC to run an independent rally. Hayes is calling for a drop with his mouth, but his long-term holdings don’t move at all. With a crafty old fox like this, let’s listen for the logic—not the panic.

He’s also put it into practice—he liquidated most of those altcoins like HYPE, NEAR, and WLD, keeping only BTC and ETH as core holdings, and moving the rest into U.S. Treasuries and energy stocks. His reasoning is that when the AI bubble is eventually popped—perhaps by high oil prices or after a few major IPOs—the capital will be forced to withdraw; only then might the Fed pivot back to easing, and money could flow back into BTC.

This sounds a bit counterintuitive, but viewed in the current situation, it actually looks pretty clear. AI stocks are still surging wildly, while BTC is just hovering around the $65,000 mark. Both sides are fighting over the same pool of money. This kind of seesaw—$BTC $ETH —is more interesting than obsessing over who’s up or down.

I’m not saying Hayes is definitely right. This is his usual style—big macro bets, not short-term signals. But one thing is worth remembering: there’s only so much money in the market. Don’t go all-in on whatever looks hot.

🚨 BREAKING NEWS 
A lot of people still think crypto scams only happen to beginners, but this case shows how convincing scammers have become.

The U.S. government has moved to seize an $ETH wallet holding around $2.12 million in USDT after investigators linked it to a large "pig butchering" investment scam. Instead of charging a person first, the government is going after the crypto itself because they believe the funds came from fraud.

The scam usually started with a simple conversation. Victims were contacted through dating apps, WhatsApp, social media, or even fake job offers. The scammers spent time building trust before introducing what looked like an amazing crypto investment opportunity with guaranteed profits.

Everything looked real. The fake investment platform even showed growing account balances, making people believe they were earning money. Seeing those fake profits convinced many victims to invest even more.

The real trap appeared when victims wanted to withdraw their money. Suddenly they were told they had to pay extra taxes, verification fees, or other charges before the withdrawal could be processed. People paid those fees hoping to unlock their profits, but the money never came back because the entire platform was fake from the beginning.

To make tracking harder, the stolen funds were moved through several Ethereum wallets. Even so, blockchain investigators followed the transactions and eventually connected the money to one wallet holding more than $2.12 million in USDT. Since the tokens were issued by Tether, authorities worked with the company to freeze the funds.

Sadly, this isn't an isolated case. Crypto investment scams continue to grow every year, and billions of dollars have already been lost. The biggest lesson is simple: if someone promises guaranteed returns, asks you to pay extra fees to withdraw your own money, or pressures you to invest more, it's almost certainly a scam. In crypto, protecting your money starts with questioning offers that seem too good to be true.

#BTC Today I’d like to briefly talk about perpetual futures. As the name suggests, they don’t have a fixed expiration date. In the current world of digital asset derivatives trading, this is actually a fairly novel type. As long as you don’t trigger liquidation and you don’t voluntarily close the position, you can keep holding it indefinitely.​​
So in real practice, how many times leverage is appropriate? I previously chatted with some friends in the industry—some people are used to opening at 50x, while others commonly use 30x. Taking one popular digital asset as an example: at 30x leverage you need a margin of 16U; at 50x it’s 10U; and at 100x only 5U is required.​​
#ETH Under the same market conditions, personally I’m more inclined to use 100x. Why? Because once you choose a leveraged contract, no matter whether it’s 1x or 100x, risk still exists. In the same market environment, the return difference between 1x and 100x is just too large. Some say 1x is safer—which is true. But for a certain popular asset, with 1x leverage, the cost per contract can be as high as more than 470U. If the price doesn’t move much, the fees alone are enough to be painful, and even if you make a profit, it’s not that much. So if you’re going to trade leveraged contracts, you should let the advantages of leverage play out fully.​​
However, you also need to be careful: many people use a small amount of capital to trade contracts beyond their capacity. If the margin isn’t enough, they simply can’t withstand market fluctuations. When the price oscillates back and forth or moves sharply up or down, it’s easy to get liquidated. After that, even if the market later turns and you could have profited, it won’t have anything to do with you anymore. That’s why for perpetual contracts, if conditions allow, preparing a bit more margin is really necessary—extra protection is always a good thing.​​
Every investment carries risk. What we should do is reduce risk as much as possible, and then pursue returns.​​
Set a small daily goal for yourself. If you achieve it, take profit in a timely way—trading will feel more composed. Friends who’ve been in this kind of trading for a while should know: if you have 5,000U in principal, earning 200–500U per day isn’t hard. If you learn some methods and techniques, your success rate can be even higher. Even considering market volatility and unexpected situations, if we take a balanced view—for a 30-day month, as long as you meet the goal on 20 days, you can still end up profitable. I hope my sharing helps everyone!

#BTC 今天简单聊聊永续合约，它就像名字说的那样，没有固定到期日，在现在的数字资产衍生品交易里，算是挺新颖的一种。只要没触发强制平仓，自己也不主动平仓，就能一直拿着。​
那实际操作中，开多少倍合适呢？之前和圈内朋友聊，有人习惯开 50 倍，也有人常用 30 倍。拿某热门数字资产来说，30 倍杠杆要 16U 保证金，50 倍得 10U，100 倍仅需 5U。​
#ETH 相同行情下，我个人更倾向 100 倍。为啥？因为一旦选了杠杆合约，不管 1 倍还是 100 倍，风险都存在。可同等行情里，1 倍和 100 倍的收益差距太大了。有人说 1 倍风险小，这确实没错，但对某热门资产来说，1 倍杠杆下，一张合约成本可能高达 470 多 U，要是价格没大波动，光手续费就够受的，就算赚了也没多少。所以既然做杠杆合约，就得让杠杆的优势充分发挥出来。​
不过得注意，很多人用少量资金做超出承受能力的合约，保证金不够，根本扛不住行情波动。遇到价格来回震荡，或者大幅涨跌，很容易被强制平仓，之后就算行情转好能盈利，也和自己没关系了。所以做永续合约，条件允许的话，多准备点保证金很有必要，多一份保障总是好的。​
任何投资都有风险，我们要做的是尽量降低风险，再去追求收益。​
每天可以给自己定个小目标，达成了就及时止盈，交易起来也会更从容。接触这类交易久的朋友应该清楚，要是有 5000U 本金，每天赚 200-500U 不算难，掌握些方法技巧，成功率还能更高。就算考虑行情波动和意外情况，折中算下来，一个月 30 天，只要 20 天达成目标，最后也能盈利。希望我的分享能帮助到大家!

So what’s the most correct trading strategy? Do nothing.

When direction is unclear, not trading is the best trade. Once you see it clearly, then act—betting blindly is always worse.

01的地基已经打好，现在开始往上盖楼
#ETH🔥🔥🔥🔥🔥🔥 $ETH $UNI 
狗哥 #hooksummer
@jingouwang888

7月29日，01的开发者连续发了两篇blog。
一篇叫"The source"——十个合约的完整源码，逐个放上网站，每一个都附带SHA-256哈希，让你不用信任任何浏览器、任何网站，自己下载、自己比对、自己验证。
另一篇叫"The foundation is set. Now it is time to build."——地基已经打好，现在开始建造。
这两篇blog放在一起读，开发者要说的只有一件事：01的基础设施阶段结束了。接下来是生态建造阶段。这不是一个计划，是一个已经发生的事实。

https://zero1.cash/blog/source
https://zero1.cash/blog/build-on-01
一、01现在是什么状态
开发者用六个模块把01当前的状态讲得清清楚楚。
代币。 ERC-20，硬顶21,000,000枚。无预售、无团队分配、无owner。新01只能通过DEX买入，bonding curve铸造的curve已打满，铸造通道永久关闭。不会再多出一枚。
储备。 流入curve的每一美元都以sUSDS形式持有，赚取Sky Savings Rate。这笔收益永远无法被提取，只用来抬高回购地板。每个持有者身后的支撑在自动上升。市值只是价格乘流通量；储备才是真实的资产支撑。
销毁。 curve上的每笔交易都销毁0.25%的手续费；卖出时curve回购的每一枚都直接销毁。铸造已关闭，没有任何东西抵消这些销毁。供应只会继续缩。
隐私池。 Zcash式设计。余额和转账关系隐藏，存款和取款公开。隐私发生在两者之间。
借贷市场。 用01做抵押借USDS。抵押品按curve的时间加权价格保守估值，不暴露你用了哪些持仓。
USD0。 1:1由USDS支撑的美元稳定币，1:1可赎回。可以公开使用，也可以进入隐私池变成私人美元。
六个模块，全部部署在ETH主网，全部上线运行。
二、开发者真正在表达什么
两篇blog的内核，拆开来看，是三层递进的信息。
第一层：信任最小化，彻底执行。
"The source"这篇blog的标题就是全部内容。十个合约，九个在Etherscan上源码验证，第十个（Poseidon hasher）是生成的字节码，通过复现来验证。开发者把所有源码打包成一个zip，附带manifest和每个文件的SHA-256哈希，放到自己的网站上。然后写了一段话：
"不要相信这个网站，也不要相信Etherscan。直接从Etherscan API拉取任何地址的验证源码，和你这里下载的文件做diff。一个免费API key就够了。"
这是01开发者对"去信任"的态度。不是口头承诺，是给你工具，让你自己验证每一个字节。
第二层：不可篡改是设计意图，不是缺陷。
blog里有一句关键的话：
"There is nothing else. No admin repository with a newer version waiting to be deployed, no upgrade proxy pointing somewhere you cannot see. The contracts below are immutable, so the source on this page describes the system as it will run forever."
没有后台仓库藏着新版本。没有升级代理指向你看不见的地方。合约不可篡改，这份源码描述的是系统永远运行的方式。
01的不可篡改性是刻意的。没有暂停按钮、没有升级路径、没有admin key。开发者自己也无法修改任何一个参数。这是一个在部署瞬间就完全交给网络的系统。
第三层：最难的部分已经完成，接下来是社区建造。
"The foundation is set"这篇blog最核心的一句：
"That is a rare place to start from. A finished, verified, permissionless private financial layer, already deployed, already owned by no one, with a real community around it. The hard part is done. What is left is building on top."
一个完成、验证、无许可的私人金融层，已经部署，已经不属于任何人，已经有了真实社区。最难的部分已经完成。剩下的是在上面建造。
开发者明确告诉所有人：01的合约层面不会再变。从现在起，01的故事不再由开发者写，而是由每一个在上面建造的人写。
三、唯一缺的那块拼图
开发者毫不回避地指出了01现在最大的短板。
隐私功能依赖零知识证明，证明的计算量较大。浏览器tab不是跑这个的地方——慢、吃内存、大多数设备跑不完。所以隐私池、隐私借贷、USD0这些需要生成证明才能使用的功能，合约端全部就绪，但用户端还不能流畅触达。
"The contracts are ready. The client is what is missing."
合约准备好了。缺的是客户端。
开发者把答案说得非常直接：一个专用的01钱包。一个真正的本地应用，在设备上持有密钥和查看密钥，从不上传到服务器，用真实算力生成证明，本地计算并显示隐私余额，通过relayer提交。合约不变、规则不变、链上什么都不变，唯一改变的是隐私交易变得可以实际操作。
"Whoever builds the first solid 01 wallet builds the front door to a private financial layer that is already finished, verified, and open."
谁先造出第一个像样的01钱包，谁就为这个已经完工、验证、开放的私人金融层建好了前门。
这是开发者给出的最明确的建造指引，也是最明确的机遇信号。
四、开发者画出的建造路线图
除了钱包，开发者还列出了其他完全开放的赛道：
能在设备上本地生成证明的移动端客户端为没有硬件条件的人提供的托管式证明服务基于公开读取接口搭建的隐私仪表盘和偿付能力页面更多由更多人运行的relayer节点，让隐私不依赖单一运营方针对隐私池的数据分析工具基于USD0的第一个私人数字银行——一个干净简洁的App，用于持有和发送有资产支撑、可赎回的私人美元
每一条都是独立的产品方向。每一条都建立在已经完工的合约之上。开发者把合约地址、读取接口、写入路径、验证包全部公开，然后说：从这里开始。
五、把01放到发展曲线上看
01从6月9日正式上线，到7月29日开发者发布这两篇blog，经历了50天。
50天里发生的事，按时间线排列：
bonding curve完成铸造，21,000,000硬顶锁死。curve上的每一笔买卖都在燃烧01，供应从打满时的20,790,000下降到当前的约19,821,851。永久离开供应的01已超过117万枚。
约182万USDS储备以sUSDS形式持有，持续赚取4-5%年化收益。收益留在合约里，只抬高回购地板。
十个合约全部在ETH主网运行，源码验证，不可篡改，无owner。
Uniswap V4主池01/ETH建立，LP手续费收益形成了社区飞轮的核心驱动。LP有收益，社区有传播理由；交易量上升，LP收益继续上升；流动性更深，新资金进入摩擦更低。
隐私池、借贷市场、USD0全部部署上线，合约端就绪。
持有地址从零增长到超过5,300+。价格从curve打满发射时的0.3到当前的接近2u，价格发现阶段。超过50%-70%以上的流通筹码被社区建设者、信仰者长期持有。
开发者现在说的是：0到1的阶段完成了。这份blog就是交接仪式——把01从"开发者建造"交到"社区建造"手中。
六、01的正面发展走势在哪里
结合开发者的blog和我对01机制的深度理解，01的正面走势沿着五条主线展开。
主线一：供应端的永久通缩已经启动，不可逆转。
铸造关闭 = 供应上限锁死。每笔curve交易燃烧0.25%。每次通过curve卖出，回购的01全部销毁。sUSDS收益抬高地板，鼓励持有而非交易，进一步减少流通。这是一台不需要任何人操作就在运转的通缩机器。
主线二：储备地板每日自动抬升。
储备金以sUSDS持有，赚取Sky Savings Rate。收益无法提取，只能抬高回购地板。分子（储备）在涨，分母（流通量）在缩，地板价格的数学走势只有一个方向。
主线三：隐私金融层的合约已经完工，等待客户端解锁。
隐私池、隐私借贷、USD0的合约全部部署完毕。当前使用率还较低，原因不是机制有问题，而是证明生成需要本地算力。一旦专用钱包上线，这些功能会同时被激活。合约层面的零变更，用户体验层面的质变。
主线四：V4 Hook赛道龙头地位持续强化。
01的核心流动性在Uniswap V4。当Hook Summer叙事继续扩散——交易所开设专区、官方基金给Grant、协议级流动性迁移进来——市场会寻找赛道里机制最完整的项目。01同时覆盖了V4 Hook、隐私金融、储备资产、LP收益四条叙事。
主线五：完全开源+无owner的结构，让01可以吸收整个社区的建造力量。
开发者把源码、哈希、验证脚本、隐私电路全部公开。任何开发者都可以读取合约状态、搭建前端、运行relayer、构建产品。01不需要一个中心化团队来推动生态——它需要的是社区识别到这个机遇并行动。开发者已经用这两篇blog明确发出了这个信号。
七、开发者没有回避的东西
blog最后有一段"Honest Status"：
"This is new, unaudited, experimental software, and the contracts cannot be patched, on purpose. There has been no external audit yet."
这是一套全新的、未经审计的实验性软件；出于设计考量，其中的合约无法进行修补。目前尚未完成外部审计。
开发者没有回避问题。这恰恰是01可信度的一部分——一个连自己的短板都公开摆出来的系统，比一个只讲好消息的项目更值得认真对待。
地基已成
01的开发者用两篇blog传递的信息可以浓缩成一句话：
合约完工了。验证完毕了。权限交出去了。从现在起，01属于每一个愿意在上面建造的人。
这就是01现在和未来的发展走势：基础设施阶段结束，生态建造阶段开始。供应在通缩，储备在增长，地板在抬升，社区在扩张。唯一缺的那块——让隐私变得好用的客户端——是下一个要攻克的方向，也是开发者明牌指出的最大机遇。
01从0到1的路走完了。接下来是从1到无穷。

In the afternoon, I was watching a single BTC transfer, waiting for confirmation. 
Suddenly I thought of a tricky question: 
Bitcoin can’t understand contract state on Ethereum at all, 
so why would BTC know whether a “loan has been repaid” or whether a “position should be liquidated”? 
Following this question, I re-read the TBV materials for @babylonlabs_io , 
and I realized the key point isn’t to force Bitcoin to ingest a smart contract. 
It’s to translate complex judgment into a result that can be executed by a script. 
When TBV is created, the parties first sign in advance the spending paths that are allowed to occur in the future, 
and then BTC is locked into a Taproot output. 
After the external protocol performs repayment or liquidation, the related state is turned into a zero-knowledge proof; 
BitVM3, using a garbled-circuit mechanism, converts “whether the proof is valid” into whether a secret can be revealed. 
For normal redemption, it follows the optimistic path, and there’s no need to move the whole computation onto Bitcoin; 
only when there’s a dispute does the challenge procedure unfold. 
Bitcoin doesn’t need to understand DeFi—
it only checks whether the final cryptographic key is correct. 
This changed my view of TBV from “an entry point for BTC收益” to “how external state obtains settlement authority over Bitcoin.” 
Each Vault corresponds to an independent UTXO; the funds don’t enter a shared pool, 
and the protocol can’t move them around arbitrarily. 
What external applications get isn’t control over BTC, 
but a verifiable, collateralized state. 
It’s still in the testing stage for now. 
The proof system, challenge-response, oracles, and emergency governance are all real risks—
don’t mistake “trustless” for “zero risk.” 
But this path is indeed tough enough: 
without moving BTC, external rules can still impose constraints on it. $BABY  #baby  #BTC #ETH

A few days ago I watched the TBV design for @babylonlabs_io  again, and it suddenly occurred to me: what the market is easiest to ignore right now isn’t whether the technology can lock up BTC; it’s whether risk can be broken down and calculated separately.
Native BTC doesn’t cross bridges, doesn’t wrap into other assets, and the private keys aren’t handed over to a custodian—which of course addresses the most direct issue of asset custody.
But once a BTC is put into Babylon, what it actually carries isn’t only the risk of the Bitcoin script.
Whether the Finality Provider votes properly, whether the Covenant Emulator enforces transactions according to the rules, whether the BSN has any erroneous states, and whether the upper-layer lending protocol can liquidate in time—all of these will affect the final outcome.
The problem is that these risks can currently be bundled into a single word: “trustless.”
A truly mature design should make users clearly see where each layer of risk comes from.
For example, if the same BTC serves multiple networks at the same time, and one network faces slashing or seizure, will it affect the other yield positions? If a particular application incurs bad debt, will losses be absorbed only within that application? When a node is down, can users still exit via the original path?
This isn’t nitpicking—it’s the foundation of risk pricing.
I agree with Babylon’s direction of turning native BTC into a usable, secure asset, but the more purposes the asset serves, the more important risk isolation becomes.
In the future, what truly determines whether TBV can scale up likely won’t be “how many applications are supported,” but whether losses can be contained within each application’s own boundaries when that application has a problem.
“Not custodial” answers who holds the coins; “isolation” answers who pays for accidents.
For $BABY , the latter may be worth focusing on long-term even more than a single word—trustless.#baby  #BTC #ETH

I follow the TBV process of @babylonlabs_io  down the line. 
The first thing I focus on isn’t returns, 
and it’s not who has more votes. 
Instead, it’s a more practical question: 
When changing parameters through governance, 
can you directly touch the native BTC in the treasury? 
Architecturally, it’s not as simple as “a vote passes, and the assets move along with it.” 
The BTC in TBV is still locked in Bitcoin UTXOs. Redemption, liquidation, and state transitions are constrained by scripts, pre-signed transactions, and proof requirements. 
BABY validators can determine protocol upgrades, application onboarding, and rule coordination, but they can’t, like ordinary DeFi governance, simply vote and then migrate users’ assets into another contract. 
With that in mind, separating BTC staking from $BABY  governance shifts the emphasis away from who’s more entitled to speak, and toward who can control which layer. 
BTC stakers obtain economic security via Finality Providers; BABY handles the control plane. 
TBV leaves the asset execution layer within Bitcoin’s rules. 
The two sides also have different unbinding/withdrawal periods, which further indicates they carry different responsibilities. 
The real risk may not come from governance directly taking BTC; it could be that governance indirectly changes proof standards, supports applications, liquidation interfaces, or security parameters. 
If the coins can’t move, it doesn’t mean the usage conditions will stay unchanged forever. 
So this design is more like splitting control into multiple layers, reducing the probability that a single governance mistake could blow through the whole system. 
But as the TBV scales up, BABY governance’s impact on the application layer will become increasingly significant. 
What’s worth watching in the future isn’t whether BTC holders have a vote, but whether they have clear exit, veto, and risk-warning mechanisms. #baby  #BTC #ETH

My judgment is: in this round of Bitcoin’s play, retail investors are no longer the main characters.

In Wintermute’s newly released OTC report for the first half of the year, institutions accounted for 72% of its over-the-counter sales— the highest ever. Six months ago it was only 61%. Retail is basically watching from the sidelines in the OTC market.

Institutions hold tight, follow risk limits and discipline. Retail, on the other hand, ends up chasing rallies and selling into drops all the way— even more pro-cyclical than institutions. The result is that volatility has been compressed from the 70% range of earlier years down to 45%, and the market action increasingly looks like “institutions playing to themselves.”

Institutions have investment committees and stop-loss lines. When it falls, they can hold through; when it rises, they don’t chase. Retail relies on sentiment: when it drops, they cut; when it rises, they surge. That’s why in bull and bear markets, the people always getting left behind are the side with more participants.

But don’t be misled by “be like the pros, hold.” Institutional holding tight doesn’t mean they’re always right. In 2022, plenty of those “long-term holders” also blew up. What ordinary people can learn isn’t stubbornly holding on—it’s setting your own lines and not betting your living expenses. Right now $BTC  is stalling above 64,000, $ETH  is hovering around the 1,900 area—institutions are quietly accumulating, so don’t panic, but don’t get carried away either.

#BTC #ETH #复盘 #Trading mindset

content:
我的判断是：这轮 Bitcoin 的玩法，散户已经不是主角了。

做市商 Wintermute 刚出的上半年 OTC 报告，机构占了它场外卖出的 72%，史上最高，半年前才 61%。散户基本在场外看戏。机构死拿、按风险限额和纪律来，散户反而一路追涨杀跌、比机构还顺周期。结果就是波动率从早年的 70% 压到了 45%，盘面越来越像机构自摸。

机构有投委会、有止损线，跌了能扛、涨了不追。散户靠情绪，一跌就割、一涨就冲，所以牛熊里被甩下车的永远是人多的那一边。

但别被'be like the pros, hold'带偏。机构死拿不等于永远对，2022 年那些'长期持有'的也爆了一茬。普通人能学的不是死扛，是给自己设条线、别拿生活费赌。现在 $BTC 在 6.4 万上方磨，$ETH 在 1900 边上晃，机构低调吸、散户别慌也别上头。

Frax proposal to charge a 4% penalty fee! Can ETH at $1,926 hold up against this wave of sell pressure?

💡 Impact on the outlook: Neutral. The 4% fee directly locks in most of the incentive to dump, so the actual sell pressure is really small.

Put simply, this proposal from the Frax community is meant to solve the long-standing headache of liquidity drying up. If you redeem frxETH early to swap back into the underlying ETH, you have to pay a 4% default penalty. This move is actually pretty smart: if you want to run, you can—but you have to leave a “toll fee” behind. That money goes straight to the treasury, subsidizing the liquidity pools where funds stay put. Right now, ETH itself is around $1,926.45, and the overall market is still hovering around $64,852.01, grinding rather than moving—liquidity is already tight. 4% isn’t huge, but for those massive whales who want to cash out anytime, it’s a pretty hard cost threshold. Essentially, it’s the project team protecting its own TVL while preventing a stampede-style bank run whenever something even slightly spooks people.

In the short term, this serves as a warning for the whole staking playbook. Previously, people were used to depositing and being able to exit instantly at zero cost. Now with a 4% exit threshold, capital’s efficiency will definitely take a hit. But if you think the other way around, this actually protects the remaining capital that hasn’t left yet. Because those willing to eat the 4% loss to retreat have mostly moved on to other higher-yield earning assets, leaving behind mainly the true believers—so the positions (chips) become more stable.

In the medium term, this track is fully entering the second half of the game: competing on underlying safety and real yield. The project teams are doing everything they can to lock up funds. Going forward, if you play similar staking protocols—whether DeFi or exchange wealth-management products—you’ll need to carefully weigh the unlock conditions and fees in advance. In today’s market, it’s not about who can paint the biggest yield promises. It’s about who can make users genuinely willing to keep their money there.

I don’t think this proposal will stir up much trouble for the broader market. The market’s core right now is whether BTC can stabilize around $64,852.01, and whether ETH can hold the psychological level at $1,926.45. A single-protocol internal rules adjustment like this can only cause minor sentiment fluctuations at most. No need to overinterpret it, and don’t blindly turn bearish on the ETH staking track. To be frank: as long as ETH itself doesn’t suffer a crash-like plunge, the 4% penalty fee is enough to hold most of the potential dump capital in place. In the short term, BTC and ETH will still follow macro liquidity flows and continue to churn and grind at the bottom.

title: 3步看懂DeFi怎么借钱：没有银行，坏账反而更难藏
subTitle:
你是不是也有这个疑问：DeFi没有银行、没有征信，凭什么敢把钱借出去？

答案很反常识：它不是更相信你，而是从一开始就不相信你。

DeFi真正要解决的，不只是“去掉中间机构”，而是用抵押和自动清算，代替传统金融里的信用。

普通银行敢放贷，是因为有征信、准备金和监管体系。链上没有这些条件，智能合约也不知道你会不会还钱，所以它只认一件事：你抵押了多少资产。

整个过程可以拆成3步。

1. 你先锁定一笔资产，比如把 $BTC 放进指定地址，链上生成对应的资产凭证。

2. 智能合约根据抵押物价值，让你借出另一种资产，比如 $ETH。资金可能来自其他用户存入的资金池。

3. 如果抵押物价格下跌，账户价值触及清算线，合约会自动处理抵押物，不需要催款，也不看你愿不愿意还。

所以，DeFi里的杠杆并不是凭空变出更多资产，而是靠“资金池＋保证金＋强制平仓”运行。它和期货、外汇中的保证金逻辑相似，只是执行者从机构变成了链上合约。

这也是看盘时需要关注 $BTC 和 $ETH 波动的原因：价格变化不仅影响涨跌，还可能触发一连串抵押物清算。行情越剧烈，合约延迟、网络阻塞和价格变化带来的风险越值得警惕。

看一个DeFi项目，别只看“去中心化”这几个字，更要看它的抵押规则、清算线、资金池，以及极端行情下能否正常执行。

真想参与，先算清自己的清算线和最坏情况，再决定是否交易。

translatedData.title: 3 Steps to Understand How DeFi Lends: With No Banks, Bad Debts Are Even Harder to Hide
translatedData.subTitle:
Do you have the same question too: with no banks and no credit reporting, how does DeFi dare to lend money out?

The answer is counterintuitive: it doesn’t trust you more—it actually doesn’t trust you from the very beginning.

What DeFi truly needs to solve is not only “removing intermediaries,” but replacing traditional finance’s credit with collateral and automatic liquidation.

Why do ordinary banks dare to issue loans? Because they have credit reporting, loan-loss reserves, and a regulatory framework. On-chain, there are no such conditions, and smart contracts also don’t know whether you’ll repay. So it only recognizes one thing: how much collateral you’ve posted.

title: CENTRAL BANK SUPER WEEK: WILL THE FED TURN HAWKISH AND SHAKE GLOBAL MARKETS?
subTitle:
Every trader watches charts, but the professionals also watch central banks.
This is one of the most important weeks for global financial markets because several major central banks are scheduled to announce their latest monetary policy decisions. 
Among them, the U.S. Federal Reserve (Fed) remains the most influential institution, with the power to move trillions of dollars across financial markets within minutes.
Whether you trade Bitcoin, Ethereum, forex, gold, stocks, or commodities, understanding how central bank decisions impact price action is essential. 
Many of the largest market moves are driven not by technical indicators alone, but by changes in monetary policy, interest rate expectations, and investor sentiment.
Why Does the Federal Reserve Matter?
The Federal Reserve is responsible for maintaining price stability and supporting maximum employment in the United States. One of its primary tools is setting interest rates.
When inflation rises too quickly, the Fed may increase interest rates to slow economic activity and reduce inflationary pressure.
When economic growth weakens or unemployment rises, the Fed may lower interest rates to encourage borrowing, spending, and investment.
Although these decisions are made for the U.S. economy, their impact extends far beyond America because the U.S.
 dollar is the world's primary reserve currency. This means the Fed's decisions influence global liquidity, capital flows, and investor confidence across virtually every financial market.
What Does "Hawkish" Mean?
A hawkish central bank focuses on controlling inflation, even if that means slowing economic growth.
A hawkish Fed typically signals: 
• Higher interest rates
 • Interest rates staying higher for longer 
• Reduced market liquidity 
• Stronger U.S. Dollar 
• Higher bond yields
 • Greater caution toward risk assets
Markets often react negatively because borrowing becomes more expensive, companies face higher financing costs, and investors tend to move capital into safer assets.
What Does "Dovish" Mean?
A dovish central bank prioritises supporting economic growth.
A dovish Fed usually suggests:
 • Lower interest rates
 • Potential future rate cuts 
• Increased liquidity 
• Weaker U.S. Dollar
 • Improved investor confidence
 • Stronger appetite for risk assets
This environment generally benefits cryptocurrencies, technology stocks, growth companies, and emerging markets because cheaper money encourages investment and speculation.
Why Should Crypto Traders Care?
Many new traders believe Bitcoin moves independently from traditional markets.
That is no longer entirely true.
Institutional investors now manage billions of pounds in digital assets through ETFs, hedge funds, pension funds, and asset management firms.
 These institutions continuously adjust portfolios based on interest rates, inflation expectations, and economic data.
When the Fed tightens monetary policy:
 • Liquidity often leaves risk assets. 
• Investors become more defensive. 
• Bitcoin and altcoins may experience increased selling pressure.
 • Market volatility usually rises.
When the Fed signals easier monetary policy:
 • Liquidity can return to financial markets. 
• Institutional demand often improves.
 • Bitcoin and high-growth assets frequently outperform.
 • Market sentiment becomes more optimistic.
This is why every serious crypto trader should pay close attention to macroeconomic developments—not just chart patterns.
What Will Traders Watch This Week?
The interest rate decision is only one piece of the puzzle.
Professional traders will also analyse:
• The wording of the FOMC statement.
 • Federal Reserve economic projections.
 • Inflation expectations. 
• Labour market outlook. 
• Future interest rate guidance. 
• Fed Chair Jerome Powell's press conference. 
• Market expectations versus the actual announcement.
Sometimes the Fed leaves rates unchanged, yet markets still experience extreme volatility because investors react to subtle changes in language or future guidance.
How Professional Traders Prepare
Experienced traders understand that preserving capital is more important than chasing every opportunity.
Before major central bank events, professionals often: 
• Reduce position sizes. • Lower leverage.
 • Protect profits. • Avoid emotional trading. 
• Wait for confirmation after the initial volatility. 
• Focus on disciplined risk management rather than predictions.
Remember, the first move after a major announcement is not always the true direction. Initial volatility can be driven by algorithms, institutional repositioning, and liquidity sweeps before the market establishes a sustained trend.
Technical Analysis Meets Macroeconomics
Technical analysis tells you where price may react.
Macroeconomic analysis helps explain why it reacts.
The most successful traders combine both approaches instead of relying on only one.
Support, resistance, liquidity zones, order blocks, and market structure become even more meaningful when they align with major macroeconomic catalysts such as Federal Reserve meetings.
Final Thoughts
Central Bank Super Week is far more than another news event—it is a reminder that financial markets are interconnected.
Whether the Federal Reserve delivers a hawkish surprise or a dovish shift, the outcome will shape investor sentiment, influence global liquidity, and potentially determine the next major trend across cryptocurrencies, equities, forex, and commodities.
Don't focus solely on predicting the announcement.m
Focus on understanding the broader economic context, managing risk effectively, and allowing price action to confirm the market's direction.
The traders who survive and thrive are not those who predict every move—they are the ones who prepare for every possible outcome.
Knowledge builds confidence. Discipline protects capital. Patience creates opportunity.

【Is a 61% drop the bottom? Sorry, I thought that way in 2017 too】

A lot of people see that ETH is down 61% from its high, and they start getting itchy, thinking, “Isn’t this when you pick up a bargain?”

Come on—let’s look at the data.

$ 1915: down 0.5% over the past 24 hours, up 1.4% over the past 7 days. 1.4%—that’s basically all the gain in a week.

So what does it mean?

It means: it doesn’t have the power. When it drops, it’s decisive; when it rises, it drags. What do you call that? Weakness. In weakness, you think it’s the bottom—most likely you’re just overthinking it.

F&G Index is 28, Fear level. All week it’s been 28, never changed. BTC’s market share is 56.6%—funds are still squeezing into BTC. ETH isn’t the main character; it’s just a supporting role that can’t rise smoothly even when it follows.

1839.69 is support, 1969.6 is resistance. If you’re stuck in the middle, you can’t go up, and you can’t go down. Volume is there, sure—someone’s trading—but it’s playing short-term, not building a big picture.

Back in 2017, the time I got cut, I also looked at the drop and thought it had fallen far enough to bounce. What happened? There was still a basement under the floor.

Now I only have one take on ETH: valuation is low, but low valuation doesn’t mean it’ll rally right away. You have to wait for BTC to lead the way, or wait for the fundamentals to bring some new story. Just buying because “it fell a lot”—I had that illness before. There’s no cure.

Next week’s focus is just one thing: can it hold above 1969.6? If it does, I’ll watch it a bit more. If it doesn’t, I’ll keep watching the show.

What’s your mindset right now? Does your finger get itchy at a position like this? Me? I’m holding back—but honestly, it’s pretty hard to.

市场情绪。资金费率0.0015%，低到几乎可以忽略。多空都在观望，没人愿意加杠杆赌方向。24h成交额75.3亿美元，这个量能放在平时算是很活跃了，但价格纹丝不动。大量资金进场却没推动价格，说明买卖力量在某个价位附近达到了短暂的平衡。这种平衡极其脆弱，通常是变盘的前奏。筹码在密集换手，只是还没人愿意先表态。

妮妮的计划。当前价 1917.84。我倾向偏空。理由很明确：大户派发量远超吸筹量，从1982下来的反弹没做出像样的力度，价格位置更靠近支撑而非阻力。1935不突破，多看少动。如果回踩1865-1870出现放量止跌信号，可以小仓位试多，止损放在1855。不急着进场。等市场自己表态。

title: Hai să vedem ce doare azi
subTitle:
Introducerea – 

Săptămâna asta, algoritmul CoinMarketCap ne spune, pe un ton foarte serios, încotro se îndreaptă banii. Evident, banii se îndreaptă exact acolo unde nu te aștepți, lăsându-te pe tine, micul investitor, cu portofoliul în mână și întrebându-te "de ce nu am cumpărat și eu asta?".
Avem trei tendințe majore: ecosistemul Binance care crește ca pe drojdie, rotația spre Layer 1 care te face să regreți că ai râs de Solana, și reglementările care, surpriză, fac bine pieței. Să le luăm pe rând, ca pe niște pastile amare.

 Ecosistemul Binance – BNB, Acțiunea Ta Preferată
Binance s-a transformat brusc în elevul model al clasei. După ce a scăpat de procesul SEC ca un personaj de film de acțiune, platforma afișează 323 de milioane de utilizatori. E mai multă lume decât populația Statelor Unite, adunată să facă stake și să vâneze airdrop-uri.
Capitalizarea ecosistemului a crescut cu 8,48% în 30 de zile, iar BNB a oferit o rentabilitate de +4,27% într-o săptămână în care Bitcoin făcea pe mortul (-0,56%). Morala? În timp ce tu te holbai la graficul BTC, banii inteligenți se mutau liniștiți în BNB. Aparent, stabilitatea și recompensele integrate sunt noul sexy.

Răzbunarea Tocilarilor.

Categoria Layer 1 a crescut cu 10,97%, dând peste nas tuturor celor care spuneau că "doar Bitcoin contează". Solana e vedeta pop a retailului, cu un scor social de 5,02 și o viteză care face orice alt blockchain să pară un melc poștal. Ethereum, în schimb, la venerabila vârstă de 11 ani, își serbează maturitatea devenind locul unde se tokenizează active reale (RWA) și alte lucruri pe care le citesc doar cei cu portofolii de milioane. 
Capitalul face rotație, căutând senzații tari. E clar: Bitcoin e "refugiul de valoare", dar Solana e locul unde mergi să te simți tânăr din nou.

 Reglementările – Când Politicienii Devin Eroi (Fără Să Vrea.

Țineți-vă bine: o știre pozitivă de la reglementatori. SEC și CFTC au decis în martie 2026 că 16 active, inclusiv $BTC , #ETH  și XRP, sunt "mărfuri digitale". Asta a eliminat incertitudinea mai ceva decât o ședință de terapie de grup, ducând la o creștere de 11,41% a acestor active.
XRP e marele câștigător, cu tranzacții medii de $85,000 care miros a bani instituționali de la o poștă. 
Acum toată lumea se uită spre legea CLARITY din Senatul SUA, care ar putea transforma această clasificare temporară în ceva permanent. Dacă trece, e posibil să vedem ETF-uri pe $SOL  și $XRP  mai repede decât poți spune "aprobare SEC". E un nou sentiment pe piață: echivalentul a afla că examenul de care îți era frică se amână pe termen nelimitat.

 Concluzia – 48 de Ore de Liniște .

Pe scurt, banii fug de Bitcoin spre ecosisteme (Binance/BNB), blockchain-uri rapide (Solana) și active cu actele în regulă (XRP). Piața trece de la frică la o lăcomie selectivă, ajutată de un cadru instituțional care, în sfârșit, pare că se trezește.
Marea întrebare pentru următoarele 48 de ore: pot #SOL  și #XRP  să-și mențină elanul în timp ce toată piața așteaptă undă verde pentru ETF-uri? Sau vom asista la clasica "buy the rumor, sell the news" care ne-a făcut pe toți mai săraci și mai înțelepți? 
Rămâneți pe recepție. Și nu uitați: DYOR, dar mai ales, nu vă luați sfaturi financiare de la cineva care folosește emoji-uri cu rachete 🚀 în mod ironic.

Interestingly, while the broader market shrank, it actually gained share—its global crypto trading volume market share rose to 10.3%, a record high. Even a dead camel is bigger than a horse: competitors may have exited and let it take share, but trading fees are still the lifeline. New ventures like the Base chain, staking, prediction markets, and the like still can’t fully make up the difference in the short term.

My take is that a company like this’s financial reports are like a thermometer for crypto activity. In a consolidation market where volume and prices both shrink and volatility stays low, businesses that rely on fees are uncomfortable. This stretch of horizontal movement—$BTC $ETH —will be carried first by exchanges. Don’t panic just because one company is losing money, and don’t get carried away just because market share hits a new high; share and profitability are two different things.

A personal firsthand story from my own surroundings:
Recently, everyone has been hearing advice from major unregulated “crypto exchanges” that they should withdraw their funds. It looks like many exchanges can’t escape the fate of this bear market—closing down, pausing services, or even running away. I have a friend. A couple of years ago, she followed her sister’s lead in Hong Kong and invested in a trading platform that was operating in Hong Kong. The name was a bit long, so I’ve forgotten it. There were celebrities endorsing it. When she pulled me in, I registered, but I didn’t invest a single cent—nothing went in. To lure people, the platform gave you 10 units of something after registration, but you had to trade up to 40 units before you could withdraw. So I used the platform’s bonus 10 units to operate with high-multiple contracts. In a bit, I got it up to 45, then I withdrew immediately. Hahahaha.

A few days later, my friend told me that the platform’s “staking” feature for their platform token was amazing—profits were very high—and she urged me to invest. She had invested 100,000. When I heard that, I thought, “Isn’t this stupid?” With my years of experience, I was sure her money would definitely be gone. I advised her: “Hurry up—withdraw as much as you can, as soon as possible. This platform doesn’t seem reliable.” She said, “Okay, okay,” but she didn’t listen. She quietly put in another 200,000.

Sure enough, within less than a month, she messaged me saying the platform couldn’t be logged into anymore… I asked what happened. She told me she lost 300,000. I was completely stunned. I said, “Weren’t you supposed to have only 100,000?” She said after I told her, she mentioned it to her sister-in-law. Her sister-in-law said, “He (that’s him—I) understands nothing. He’s a mainland ‘northwest’ guy with no exposure—what kind of world has he seen? How many days has he even spent in the crypto space?” She continued, “I’m in Hong Kong. How could he know more about whether it’s reliable? There are ads all over the place—celebrities invested too, and they were the ones endorsing it. You should stay away from people like that who have no knowledge and no perspective.” Hahahaha. That’s what she told me.

And the result? Her sister-in-law also invested several million, and even took out loans. After hearing that one sentence, I didn’t say anything. الصورة العامة اليوم إيجابية بحذر لكلا الأصلين. BTC يبدو أكثر ثباتًا كمؤشر على معنويات السوق، بينما ETH يبقى جذابًا من ناحية الحركة، لكنه غالبًا أكثر حساسية للتذبذب. لذلك المقارنة اليوم ليست من الأفضل إلى الأسوأ، بل بين ثبات نسبي في BTC ومرونة وحساسية أكبر في ETH.

#baby $BABY I recently went out of my way to dig through the node and staking code for @babylonlabs_io . I originally meant to trace the withdrawal logic, but unexpectedly I got stuck at the “Covenant Committee” here. Let’s also talk about the topics #baby  and $BABY : a project that focuses on pure, “no-frills” plain-vanilla operations—where users manage their own private keys—why does it still need an intermediate organization? Is it just unnecessary overengineering, or is it a hard requirement?

At first, I genuinely thought this diluted the “purity” of decentralization. But after going deeper into the technical logic, I understand: it’s essentially an engineering workaround forced out when Bitcoin’s underlying code isn’t sufficient.

The limitation at the base layer: although Babylon runs on Taproot and UTXO, the native scripts available to Bitcoin aren’t capable of fully and automatically enforcing a “freeze/trigger” for withdrawals and the associated slashing/penalty flows.

A multisig solution to break the deadlock: to prevent funds from going all over the place, the only way is to require a certain number of participants to jointly sign, tightly constraining the movement path of BTC.

What moved me most is how thoroughly it separates “asset control”:

For a normal unlock, you must have the signer process: you personally confirm together with the multisig organization, then wait for a fixed number of blocks before you can use the principal. If someone behaves maliciously and triggers a penalty event, that organization also can’t take away a single coin with any “twist of intent.” They are just “emotionless trigger devices”—they can only execute the fixed code that was written in advance, routing a fixed proportion of the coins into a pre-defined black hole. This is delegated execution, absolutely not customer custody.

In short, Babylon has done something that crosses the niche boundary: it doesn’t rely on cross-chain bridges, and it doesn’t issue derivative tokens. It directly uses plain Bitcoin as the moat for PoS. Sure, the multisig and scripting approach may feel a bit cumbersome right now, but I’m more excited about how it could evolve. If one day the Bitcoin mainnet truly unlocks stronger contract constraint capabilities, this transitional organization can fully retire. Everything happening now is essentially a wooden bridge built on the way to the endgame. #eth $ETH

刚开始，我真以为这在拉低去中心化的纯度。但深挖技术逻辑后，我明白了：这纯属比特币底层代码不够用时，逼出来的工程方案。

底层限制：虽然 Babylon 跑在 Taproot 和 UTXO 上，但大饼现有的原生脚本根本没能力全自动卡死提款和惩罚流程。

多签破局：为了不让资金乱飞，只能靠凑齐一定数量的人来联合签字，死死框住 BTC 的移动路线。

拿正常的解锁来说，必须要你本人加上多签组织一起确认，再等完固定的区块时间才能动用本金。若是有人作恶触发罚没，这个组织也休想动一分钱歪心思。他们仅仅是“没有感情的触发器”，只能按提前写好的代码，把固定比例的币打进预设黑洞。这叫代为执行，绝对不叫代客托管。

总而言之，Babylon 做成了一件破圈的事：不依赖跨链桥、不造衍生币，直接拿大饼给 PoS 当护城河。虽然现在看这套多签和脚本有些繁琐，但我更期待未来的演进。倘若有一天大饼主网真的解锁了更强悍的合约约束力，这个过渡性质的组织就能彻底功成身退了。眼下这一切，其实就是奔向终局前搭的一座木桥。#eth $ETH

#baby $BABY Recently, I’ve calmed down and gone through the complete underlying mechanics of @babylonlabs_io . My original intention was to figure out the real withdrawal path for the big pie. But instead, I got stuck obsessing over the setting of the Covenant Committee (contract committee). Borrowing the momentum around #baby  and $BABY , I also want to explore my original question: a protocol that calls itself “native” and “self-custodied,” yet somehow creates this third-party role—doesn’t that amount to indirectly manufacturing trust risks?

After digging into the technical documentation, I found that this is not a compromise, but a “sober workaround” under the current technological bottlenecks.

This is by no means the project team trying to centralize power. It’s simply a helpless move constrained by today’s Bitcoin base-layer capabilities. Although the protocol’s transactions are built on Taproot and UTXO, the scripts are still too rudimentary to independently close the loop on all the complex logic of unbonding and penalties. If the underlying framework can’t meet the requirements, then you have to introduce a multi-signature threshold mechanism. By coordinating authorization among members, BTC is locked firmly onto a predefined track, preventing assets from going off course.

What truly puts me fully at ease is its logic for isolating asset permissions:

Compliant exit: The staker must cooperate with the committee to gather the required signatures and survive the specified timelock before they can get their principal back.

Unauthorized severe punishment: If a penalty is triggered, the committee also can’t put the money into their own pockets. They’re just a “cold-trigger,” executing only what the hard-coded code allows. How much is deducted and which black-hole address it’s sent to are all decided in advance—they don’t have any freedom to touch or transfer funds.

In short, Babylon’s biggest contribution is that it holds the line against cross-chain transfers and packaged assets, hard-baking Bitcoin into a safety foundation for PoS chains. To achieve this, the coordination mechanism introduced today may look a bit cumbersome, but I’m more excited about its long-term development: once, in the future, Bitcoin itself supports stronger native smart contract functionality, this committee can be gloriously laid off anytime. For now, this architecture is simply an excellent stepping stone toward the final perfect form.#eth $ETH

深入技术文档后，我发现这并非妥协，而是当前技术瓶颈下的“曲线救国”。

这绝不是项目方想搞集权，而是受限于当前比特币底层能力的无奈之举。虽然协议的交易都构建在 Taproot 和 UTXO 之上，但目前的脚本太原始，没法靠自己闭环整个解约和惩罚的复杂逻辑。既然底层框架达不到要求，就只能引入一个多签门槛机制。通过成员联合授权，把 BTC 死死锁在预设的轨道上，防止资产跑偏。

真正让我完全放心的，是它对资产权限的隔离逻辑：

合规离场： 质押方必须配合委员会凑齐签名，并熬过规定的时间锁，才能拿回自己的本金。

违规重罚： 万一触发惩罚，委员会也休想把钱装进自己的口袋。他们不过是个“无情的触发器”，只能顺着写死的代码执行操作。扣多少钱、打给哪个黑洞地址，全都是提前定死的，他们根本没有随意触碰和转移资金的权限。

总的来说，Babylon 最大的贡献，就是守住了不跨链、不搞包装资产的底线，硬是把比特币盘活成了 PoS 链的安全基石。虽然为了实现这点，当下引入的这套协调机制看着有些繁琐，但我更期待它的长线发展：一旦未来比特币自身支持了更强大的原生智能合约功能，这个委员会随时可以光荣下岗。眼下的这套架构，不过是通向最终完美形态的一座绝佳跳板而已。#eth $ETH

Hardware Wallet Shocks With a Major Case! 594 BTC Stolen — Can Cold Wallets Still Be Trusted?

One sentence to explain it clearly
Coinkite issues an urgent emergency warning: Coldcard Mk3 has a serious vulnerability. To date, 594 BTC has been stolen. All old users must transfer their assets immediately.

What happened
Guys, honestly, this is pretty terrifying to hear. A well-known hardware wallet manufacturer, Coinkite, suddenly issued an emergency alert, calling out its older device, the Coldcard Mk3, for a serious security flaw. In plain terms: hackers exploited a gap in the device’s security mechanism. A bunch of users have already fallen victim, and a total of 594 BTC has been lost. At current coin prices, that’s over a hundred million dollars’ worth of real value evaporating directly.

The official response is frantic, and the “survival plan” they provide is both simple and blunt: all old-timers still using Mk3 must immediately add a strong, independent BIP-39 passphrase on the device, then transfer all coins to newly generated wallet addresses. Don’t drag your feet—because the next account that gets wiped could be yours.

Impact on the market
- Short term: This is a pure black-swan event, definitely negative for market sentiment. Although BTC and the broader market haven’t crashed yet, once the message spreads that “even cold wallets aren’t safe,” retail traders’ instinctive defense is to take coins out of both software and hardware wallets and rush them to exchanges to sell and hedge. This can create short-term selling pressure, and panic-driven funds may briefly exit the market.
- Mid term: It will trigger a trust crisis across the crypto space regarding hardware wallets. People will start doubting the so-called “absolutely secure cold wallets.” Funds on the industry side may also face a period of pain. This, in turn, forces hardware manufacturers to upgrade their underlying security architecture, and the negative sentiment in the industry needs time to digest.

My take
My view is very clear: bearish in the short term—don’t catch falling knives at this level. Sudden events that spark risk-avoidance sentiment usually transmit to the price action within a few hours. At that point, institutions usually won’t allow shorts to expand without limit; instead, they tend to quickly squeeze shorts, force a short-covering rally, and support the market to prevent panic from turning into a chain-reaction stampede.

So, the so-called “bailout” lately is essentially not meant to make the market rise immediately, but to control the speed of the decline and stabilize the leverage system.

Wall Street isn’t crypto, and it isn’t “mainland A-shares.” It has zero tolerance for short sellers.
